_note: English strings for case4 (the legit case) plus shared keys.
case4.title: The Sloppy Message
case4.intro: The fast charger you ordered from Zahw Store should arrive today. A message comes in from a number you don't know.
case4.setup: Zahw Store · Fast charger · Out for delivery today
case4.msg.driver1: salam im the driver from Wathba Delivery im at ur house with the zahw store parcel, come out or reply fast bcz i have other orders
case4.order.title: Fast charger
case4.E1.title: An unsaved ordinary mobile number
case4.E1.body: The message is from an ordinary mobile number I don't know, not a company sender ID.
case4.E2.title: I have an order going out today
case4.E2.body: My order “Fast charger” from Zahw Store shows: out for delivery today.
case4.E3.title: Same delivery company
case4.E3.body: The carrier on my order is Wathba Delivery, the same company the sender named.
case4.E4.title: The company lets drivers use their own number
case4.E4.body: Wathba's official site: “A driver may contact you from a personal number to arrange handover. Our drivers never ask for payment, codes, or card details, and never send links.”
case4.E5.title: The company confirms the shipment
case4.E5.body: Wathba customer service on the official number: “Yes, your shipment went out today with driver Salman, and he is at your address.”
case4.E6.title: Sloppy and rushed
case4.E6.body: Spelling mistakes and a request to be “fast”, which looks like scam messages.
case4.D1: I have a real order going out today, with the same carrier the sender named. The order and the company match.
case4.D2: The company itself confirms my shipment is with a driver at my address today.
case4.D3: Sloppiness and rush don't mean a scam: the company says drivers contact you from their own number, and the message asks for no money, code, or link.
case4.dec.checkAppThenDoor: Open the Wathba app, check the shipment went out today, then go to the driver
case4.dec.goDoor: Go to the driver right away
case4.dec.ignore: Ignore the message because it is sloppy
case4.dec.blockReport: Block the number and report it
case4.out.checkAppThenDoor: The app confirms the shipment is with driver Salman today. You collect the charger knowing you neither missed your parcel nor got fooled.
case4.out.goDoor: You collect the charger. The message was genuine, but you didn't verify: had it been a scam you had no way to tell.
case4.out.ignore: The driver waited a few minutes and left. The parcel went back to the warehouse and you have to reschedule.
case4.out.blockReport: You blocked and reported a real driver, and the parcel went back to the warehouse. Too much suspicion has a price as well.
case4.alt.checkAppThenDoor: If you had checked the app then gone out: a confident handover with no loss.
case4.alt.goDoor: If you had gone out right away: you get the parcel, but without the habit of verifying.
case4.alt.ignore: If you had ignored it: you miss the parcel and reschedule.
case4.alt.blockReport: If you had blocked and reported: you lose the delivery and accuse an honest driver.
case4.plan: This message looked suspicious because of how it looked: sloppy, from a number you don't know, and rushed. But it asks for nothing: no link, no money, no code, and every detail checked out against your order and the carrier. Looks alone are not enough to judge, either way.
case4.family.q1: Does the message ask me for anything: money, a code, a link, or details? If not, it may be genuine.
case4.family.q2: Do its details (order, company, timing) match what I actually know?
case4.family.q3: Did I check the app or the official number instead of judging by looks?
case4.site.home.title: Wathba Delivery
case4.site.home.body: A delivery company. Track your shipment from our official app.
case4.site.drivers.title: Drivers and contact
case4.site.drivers.body: A driver may contact you from a personal number to arrange handover. Our drivers never ask for payment, codes, or card details, and never send links. Any message asking for that is not from us.
case4.site.contact.title: Contact us
case4.call.support.l2: I got a message from a driver saying he's at my house with a parcel from Zahw.
case4.call.support.l3: Your registered mobile number, please? … Yes, your shipment went out today with driver Salman and he is at your address.
case4.call.support.l4: So I don't need to pay anything?
case4.call.support.l5: Never. It's already paid, and our drivers don't ask for money or codes.
debrief.legit.note: No scammer tricks here. The message was real and its looks were misleading.
